observations: This profile groups KB-014..KB-024 (feature_id=FEAT-ORDER-PORTAL-01 in the upstream KB) plus KB-001 (general order/order-item structure overview, feature_id blank upstream but thematically part of 'reviewing an order' here) around the single user goal 'a merchant reviews an incoming order and initiates fulfillment', not as a flat list of portal pages/endpoints.
Every field below traces to at least one kb_id from candidate/product-kb.json. No new knowledge, rule, or expected behavior was introduced beyond what that KB states.
All behavior is carried at knowledge_kind OBSERVED_CURRENT — nothing upgraded to CONFIRMED_EXPECTED; there is no authority source in this ZERO_DOC_BOOTSTRAP run.

KB-022 ('Confirm & Send to fulfill' triggers no mutation, dialog is read-only review) is preserved here SCOPED STRICTLY to the POD-disconnected instance state observed. The POD-connected branch is treated only as a dependency/risk/unknown, never generalized into a capability or state-transition statement of its own.

KB-CONFLICT-001 (order JTEL87JY0 never appeared in portal Orders; user's webhook-fix claim unverified) is carried into this profile's risks/dependencies exactly as UNRESOLVED, per contract §8 — not resolved here. It is treated as a merchant-facing risk: an order could silently fail to reach this feature's entry point at all.
unknowns: Whether an order can silently fail to reach the portal Orders list (KB-CONFLICT-001) is UNRESOLVED — this feature's entry point assumes the order is already visible, which is not guaranteed.
Whether 'Confirm & Send to fulfill' triggers any mutation / real POD API call once Printify (or another POD) IS connected is completely UNKNOWN — never observed.
Whether 'Change status' dropdown transitions, and the 'Bulk Fulfill' page, have any side effects is completely UNKNOWN — neither was exercised.

feature_profiles.name: Review and initiate fulfillment for an incoming order
feature_profiles.user_goal: As a merchant (owner), review an order that has come in through the storefront, inspect its items/customization/status, and initiate the fulfillment review step.

actors.permission_observed: Full observed access to orders list, order-details, item activity logs, fulfill dialog, and the change-status dropdown (view only, no transition executed). No other role/permission level (e.g. staff, limited/non-owner) was tested in this run, so no permission BOUNDARY has been observed — only what this one role can do.

entry_points.path: portal Orders list (portal/orders) -> order-details (order #1002 / id 4322) -> 'Confirm & Send to fulfill' button
entry_points.precondition: Order must already be visible in the portal Orders list (GET /api/orders?by_teeinblue=1) — this precondition is NOT always guaranteed to hold; see risks[0] / KB-CONFLICT-001. There is no separate 'portal/fulfills' route: fulfillment review is only reachable via a specific order's detail page.

capabilities.name: Browse and locate orders in the portal orders list
capabilities.description: Orders list defaults to date range 'Aug 14 - Sep 13', Store 'Any', TIB Status 'Any', backed by GET /api/orders?by_teeinblue=1&cursor=&per_page=25&sort=created_at&sort_type=desc. Search matches the internal order 'name' (e.g. '#1002') but does NOT match the Shopify checkout confirmation code (e.g. 'JTEL87JY0') even for a synced order — these are separate identifier namespaces in this system.

capabilities.name: Review order and order-item structure and details
capabilities.description: An Order contains one or more Order Items, each with its OWN status badge (independent from the order-level tib_status badge), its own campaign/variant/customization/design, and an attached POD service (e.g. Printify). For the single order observed: header shows '#1002 (#-4322)', tib_status badge 'ready', creation timestamp rendered in America/New_York; the order item ('#-6957') shows item-level status 'Ready', Shopify SKU distinct from Fulfilled SKU, Shopify fulfillment status empty, fulfillment service 'manual', a Customization block (View/Edit, never exercised), and Designs data (mockup, artwork name, printarea 'front' 12x18 at 3600x5400px — notably higher resolution than the on-screen preview). A separate 'Fulfillment Shipping method' panel (order/instance-level, distinct from the Shopify checkout shipping choice) showed 'No shipping method' configured. Notes/Customer/Shipping/Billing panels mirror the data entered at Shopify checkout.

capabilities.name: Cross-check order status between UI and API
capabilities.description: For the same order at the same point in time, the portal UI badge 'ready' corresponds to API field tib_status = integer 6 (REST GET /api/orders) and the same-named field exists on the GraphQL orders_by_pk query (field name only, no raw payload captured). This is the ONLY UI-label/integer pairing observed in this run; no other tib_status value has been seen.

capabilities.name: Review automatic item activity log
capabilities.description: The 'Item Activity Logs' dialog for an order-item shows a fully automatic event sequence with no manual merchant action: line item created -> generating a design -> design generated (with printarea/artwork/artwork-version identifiers) -> marked 'Ready to fulfill', all within ~22 seconds of order creation.

capabilities.name: Initiate fulfillment review via 'Confirm & Send to fulfill' — POD-disconnected instance only
capabilities.description: On an instance where the POD provider (Printify) is NOT connected, clicking 'Confirm & Send to fulfill' opens a REVIEW dialog (not an immediate submission) showing the line item/printareas/status/shipping address with a 'Close' action and a 'Connect' prompt for Printify — no submit/pay action is available. Only 2 read-only GraphQL re-fetches (orders_by_pk, order_item_activities) were observed around the click; no mutation and no network call to a POD provider occurred. THIS FINDING IS SCOPED STRICTLY TO THE POD-DISCONNECTED STATE and describes what happens BEFORE any real send-to-fulfill submission could occur — it says nothing about what happens once a POD account is connected (see dependencies/risks).

capabilities.name: View (not execute) order-item status change options
capabilities.description: The order-item-level 'Change status' dropdown lists 5 options (Ready, Sent, Fulfilled, Paused, Canceled). No option was selected in this run — this capability is limited to what the dropdown DISPLAYS; no transition, endpoint, or side effect has been observed.

state_transitions.condition: order must already be present in the list result set
log entries are pre-existing/automatic, generated at order-creation time, not generated by opening the dialog

state_transitions.to: fulfill review dialog open (read-only, Connect prompt shown)
state_transitions.condition: OBSERVED ONLY for POD-disconnected state; no submit action available; no mutation fired. The transition to an actual 'sent to fulfillment' state was NEVER reached or observed in this run, in either POD-connected or POD-disconnected branches.

observed_behavior.statement: Order-level status badge and order-item-level status badge are independently tracked and can display different labels ('ready' vs 'Ready').
Order timestamps render in America/New_York regardless of the buyer's checkout timezone (UTC).
Design print resolution (3600x5400px) is substantially higher than the on-screen mockup preview.
Item activity log events fire automatically post-order-creation with no merchant action required.
'Confirm & Send to fulfill' does not immediately submit; it opens a review dialog first, at least in the POD-disconnected state observed.
There is no dedicated 'portal/fulfills' route; fulfillment review is reached only through a specific order's detail page.

permissions.note: Only this single role was exercised against every capability in this feature. No non-owner or restricted-permission role was tested, so no access boundary is known.

api: APIOP-006 (GraphQL call observed at fulfill-click, read-only)

dependencies: Depends on FEAT-ORDER-01 successfully placing AND syncing an order into the portal — this handoff is not guaranteed reliable (see risks[0] / KB-CONFLICT-001).

The true behavior of 'Confirm & Send to fulfill' depends on POD (Printify) connection state. Only the POD-disconnected branch is known (KB-022); the POD-connected branch is an unresolved dependency for any test or automation that assumes 'no mutation is fired' generally.

risks.risk: An order placed via storefront checkout may silently fail to appear in the portal Orders list, blocking this feature's entry point entirely.
risks.detail: Order JTEL87JY0 never appeared in GET /api/orders?by_teeinblue=1 across 90+ minutes, all TIB statuses, both stores, and a 30-day range. A later order (portal id 4322, used throughout this profile) DID appear, after the user claimed a webhook-config fix. That claim was NOT independently verified by this exploration (no dev/infra log access in this run) — it must be treated as an unverified user statement, not a confirmed fix. Resolution: UNRESOLVED (KB-CONFLICT-001), decidable only by orchestrator + context-quality-reviewer. Impact for this feature: a merchant may believe no order exists / lose track of a real order with no visible portal signal.

risks.risk: 'Confirm & Send to fulfill' behavior with a CONNECTED POD account (e.g. Printify) is completely unobserved.
risks.detail: KB-022's 'review dialog only, no mutation, no POD network call' finding is scoped strictly to the POD-DISCONNECTED state observed in this run. It must NOT be treated as a general safety property of this action. Once a POD account is connected, this click may trigger a real mutation and/or an outbound call to the POD provider (potentially a real production side effect) — this is unknown and unverified, not confirmed-safe.

risks.risk: 'Change status' dropdown transitions and 'Bulk Fulfill' are entirely unexercised and may have unknown side effects (notifications, POD calls, irreversible state changes).

unknown_areas.question: Is the storefront->portal order sync now durably fixed, or could an order silently fail to appear again?
unknown_areas.why_it_matters: This feature's entry point assumes the order is already visible in the portal; if sync can silently fail, this whole feature becomes unreachable for the affected order with no error surfaced to the merchant.

unknown_areas.question: What happens when 'Confirm & Send to fulfill' is clicked on an instance with Printify (or another POD) actually connected — does it fire a mutation, call the POD API, or create a real fulfillment/purchase order?
unknown_areas.why_it_matters: This is the single biggest gap for safe test/automation design: the only observed behavior (no mutation) is scoped to a state (POD disconnected) that real merchants using this feature for its actual purpose would not be in.

unknown_areas.question: What are the full 'Change status' dropdown option effects (Ready/Sent/Fulfilled/Paused/Canceled) — target endpoint, allowed transitions, side effects (notifications, POD calls)?
unknown_areas.why_it_matters: Only the option LIST was seen; no transition was ever executed. Any regression checklist must not assume any transition is safe, reversible, or has no side effect.

unknown_areas.question: What does 'Bulk Fulfill' (sidebar flyout item) do?
unknown_areas.why_it_matters: Never opened in this run. Its behavior is completely unknown and must not be inferred from the single-order 'Confirm & Send to fulfill' flow — it may operate at a different (higher-risk, multi-order) scope.

unknown_areas.question: Does 'portal/fulfills' exist as any kind of route elsewhere in the app (e.g. under a different nav path not explored), or is order-details truly the only entry point?
unknown_areas.why_it_matters: Only the visible sidebar was checked in this run; absence of evidence is not proof of absence for every possible route.

unknown_areas.question: What is the full tib_status enum and its integer<->label mapping, and what triggers each transition?
unknown_areas.why_it_matters: Only one value pair (ready/6) was observed for one order; do not build validation or transition tests assuming a known, exhaustive enum.

unknown_areas.question: Does any non-owner / restricted-permission portal role see the same orders list, order-details, and fulfill/status actions as the owner (sub=273)?
unknown_areas.why_it_matters: No permission boundary has been tested; access-control regressions on this feature are currently untestable from this profile alone.

unknown_areas.question: What is the true raw payload of GET /api/orders and GraphQL orders_by_pk for this order (both referenced capture files are missing on disk)?
unknown_areas.why_it_matters: KB-016/KB-018 field shapes are UI/name-only, not payload-verified — schema-level assertions should not be built on them yet.

unknown_areas.question: What were the 3 unidentified network entries observed around the 'Confirm & Send to fulfill' click (out of 5 total, only 2 matched to known GraphQL operations)?
unknown_areas.why_it_matters: They were not confirmed benign/unrelated; an unidentified call near a fulfillment action deserves scrutiny before this action is treated as fully understood.

unknown_areas.question: What do 'Edit customization' / 'View customization' actually do for the merchant?
unknown_areas.why_it_matters: Never exercised; unknown whether merchant edits here affect the design, the order, or trigger any downstream regeneration.

profile_relationships.description: FEAT-ORDER-PORTAL-01's entry point (an order visible in the portal Orders list) depends on FEAT-ORDER-01's checkout-to-sync handoff, which is not guaranteed reliable — see KB-CONFLICT-001.

orders list REST + order-details GraphQL field names

GET /api/orders?by_teeinblue=1 never returned JTEL87JY0 across 90+ minutes / all statuses / both stores / 30-day range; only the later order (id 4322, the one used throughout this profile) ever appeared.

profile_change_summary: Initial version. No prior feature profile existed for FEAT-ORDER-PORTAL-01 before this bootstrap run.

conditions: KB-022 ('no mutation on Confirm & Send to fulfill') must remain scoped to the POD-disconnected state in all downstream use (checklists, diffs); the POD-connected branch must be treated as unknown, not as 'presumably also safe'.

KB-CONFLICT-001 must remain UNRESOLVED in downstream consumption until orchestrator/reviewer decide otherwise; it must be surfaced as a merchant-facing risk (order may not appear in portal), not silently dropped.
'Bulk Fulfill' and 'Change status' transitions are unexercised; any checklist derived from this profile must list them as coverage gaps, not as low-risk/implicitly-tested areas.

This profile rests on exactly one order, one line item, one role (owner sub=273), one environment (staging) — do not generalize the tib_status enum, field shapes, or permission model beyond what was observed.
